newsitem.title: USA: Great Lakes Aviation grounds flights.
newsitem.headline: Great Lakes Aviation grounds flights.

text.p: A commuter carrier for United and Midway Airlines grounded flights after federal inspectors found it operated "unairworthy aircraft," the Federal Aviation Administration said on Saturday.

Great Lakes Aviation Ltd, based in Spencer, Iowa, voluntarily agreed to suspend operations on Friday after the FAA told the carrier it planned to suspend its operating authority, the regulatory agency said in a statement.
"The FAA does not hesitate to take swift action to protect the safety of the flying public," said Barry Valentine, acting FAA administrator.

The company operates as Great Lakes Airlines and, under agreements with United Airlines and Midway Airlines, as United Express and Midway Connection. It runs 500 flights a day and carries about 887,000 passengers annually, the FAA said.
"Great Lakes is taking this voluntary step to insure that there is no question as to the safe operation of its flights," the company said in a statement.
It said all flights had been canceled through Tuesday and that affected passengers would be rebooked on other carriers.

The FAA said it stepped up surveillance of Great Lakes' maintenance operations on April 29 after the agency's Des Moines office found the airline allowed personnel who were not properly trained and qualified to perform aircraft maintenance.
"The FAA alleges that the airline operated unairworthy aircraft," the statement said.
Great Lakes Aviation has a fleet of 53 twin-engine turboprop aircraft. It offers service to 82 cities across the United States and three cities in Mexico.

The FAA said its action was not related to last November's accident in Quincy, Illinois, when a Great Lakes-operated United Express plane collided with a small aircraft, killing 14 people. It was Great Lakes' first crash in more than 20 years of operation.

Last month, the company reported a net loss for 1996 of $12.8 million, due in part to a special charge of $1.5 million to write down the value of its spare parts inventory. In March, Great Lakes said it was experiencing liquidity difficulties and was in talks with creditors.
